stories.body: A heavy overnight Russian missile barrage killed at least nine people in Kyiv and the surrounding region, Ukrainian authorities said, with at least 33 others injured. Strikes damaged residential buildings, warehouses, a medical facility, a children's hospital, an educational institution and an industrial site, while rescuers searched rubble for survivors. The assault also prompted Poland to activate defensive air operations and Romania to scramble aircraft after a drone entered its airspace and crashed in an uninhabited area.
stories.headline: Russian missile barrage kills at least nine people in Kyiv

stories.body: President Donald Trump said the United States would impose “tremendous economic consequences” on any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities provide Iran with a lifeline. He offered no details on the prospective measures, but his statement appeared to signal an escalation of Operation Economic Fury, Washington's effort to isolate Tehran through sanctions and a naval blockade. The threat could particularly affect China, Iran's largest oil customer, and comes amid a deadlock in efforts to end the US-Israel war with Iran.
stories.headline: Trump threatens economic punishment for countries that support Iran

stories.body: More than 100 people were killed when an artisanal gold mine collapsed after a landslide in Zamboye, western Central African Republic, near the Cameroon border. Rescuers continued recovering bodies and searching for survivors, with local officials warning that the death toll could rise because many people remained trapped and the number working in the mine was unknown. Authorities opened an investigation, while officials said the collapse may have involved several underground tunnels.
stories.headline: More than 100 killed in Central African Republic gold mine collapse

stories.body: Israel's military has acknowledged that its troops fired at the vehicle carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab and six relatives in Gaza in January 2024, and said it would open a criminal investigation into their deaths and the killing of two paramedics sent to rescue her. Rajab survived the initial attack and spent hours pleading for help by phone before contact was lost; the ambulance dispatched with Israeli coordination was also hit. The military had previously denied troops were in the area, though later investigations pointed to nearby Israeli forces.
stories.headline: Israel acknowledges soldiers fired at car in which Hind Rajab was killed and opens investigation

stories.body: US gross national debt has exceeded $40 trillion for the first time, Treasury data showed, more than doubling from just under $20 trillion a decade ago. The total reached about $40.05 trillion on 18 August, earlier than Congressional Budget Office forecasts, after years of deficit spending, pandemic borrowing and rising interest costs under both Trump and Biden administrations. The milestone has intensified concern over future borrowing costs, with the debt ceiling near $41.1 trillion and the CBO projecting debt could reach about $64 trillion by 2036.
stories.headline: US national debt surpasses $40 trillion

stories.body: Freedom Caucus-backed candidates suffered broad losses in Wyoming's Republican primaries, including the defeat of the state caucus chair, Rachel Rodriguez-Williams, in the secretary of state race, as well as losses in legislative, superintendent and treasurer contests. The defeats add to recent setbacks for prominent Freedom Caucus-aligned candidates in Florida, Tennessee, Texas and South Carolina. Wyoming moderates said voters rejected an agenda they viewed as extreme and driven by outside groups, while the state Freedom Caucus said it would continue its work.
stories.headline: Wyoming Republican primaries deliver setback to Freedom Caucus candidates

stories.body: Los Angeles police officer Daniel Flores will not face felony charges over recordings he made of colleagues' offensive comments. Prosecutors had faced backlash over the case, with critics warning that pursuing felony charges against an officer who documented alleged misconduct could discourage future police whistleblowers.
stories.headline: Los Angeles police whistleblower will not face felony charges over recording colleagues

stories.body: Spain's government plans to move 500 migrant children, most of them girls, from Ceuta to the mainland after tens of thousands of people crossed into the Spanish North African enclave at the end of July. The move reverses the interior minister's earlier assertion that those entering illegally would be returned to Morocco and has intensified political disagreement, with the conservative People's Party calling for returns. The government says returning children is illegal unless their best interests are guaranteed, including proper assessment and safe family reunification conditions.
stories.headline: Spain plans to move 500 migrant children from Ceuta to the mainland amid a deepening political dispute

stories.body: Granada and its metropolitan area experienced a series of further earthquakes after Tuesday's magnitude 4.8 tremor, with the National Geographic Institute recording six overnight shocks, five of which residents reported feeling. A new magnitude 3.4 earthquake struck near Dílar at a depth of about five kilometres. The province remains in a seismic episode that began on 14 August and has included two magnitude 4.8 quakes, prompting inspections of affected buildings and earlier evacuations in several localities.
stories.headline: Granada shaken by a series of aftershocks following Tuesday's 4.8-magnitude earthquake

stories.body: Spain's weather agency issued warnings across 13 regions, including a highest-level red alert in the Valencian Community where temperatures were forecast to reach 43°C to 44°C. Orange warnings for intense heat, storms or rain were in force in Aragón, Andalusia, Castilla-La Mancha, Murcia and Catalonia. Temperatures reached 44.1°C in Xàtiva and 43.6°C in Carcaixent, while Valencia recorded 42.7°C, leading authorities to extend pool hours, alter outdoor work schedules and take additional fire precautions.
stories.headline: Extreme heat warnings issued across Spain, with Valencia expected to reach 44°C

stories.body: A wildfire in the Las Hurdes area of Cáceres remained out of control and spread into Salamanca province, prompting authorities to order the confinement of Nuñomoral, a town of about 1,200 residents, because of advancing flames and smoke. Around 700 people had already been evacuated from 10 hamlets, along with residents and staff from a care centre. Officials said the blaze, believed in early inquiries to have been deliberately started, had developed difficult fire-driven weather conditions, including pyrocumulus clouds and flare-ups.
stories.headline: Las Hurdes wildfire spreads into Salamanca province as evacuations and confinement orders continue

stories.body: Barcelona has experienced an exceptionally hot summer so far, with data from the Fabra Observatory showing average nighttime temperatures 3.3°C above the climatic norm and average daytime highs 4.6°C above normal between 1 June and 19 August. Of 80 days assessed, 72 had minimum temperatures above their usual average, while the average maximum was 32.24°C. Catalonia has also recorded a new high of 20 days this year with temperatures reaching at least 40°C somewhere in the region.
stories.headline: Barcelona records an exceptionally hot summer, with nights 3.3°C and days 4.6°C above normal

stories.body: The Port of Barcelona is building a third vehicle terminal to accommodate growing imports of Chinese cars and reinforce its role as a distribution hub for southern Europe. Vehicle traffic reached 386,000 in the first half of the year, with imports up 36% and China accounting for roughly half of arriving vehicles. The automated, all-electric terminal is due to be completed by the end of 2027 and begin operating in 2028, with capacity for up to 12,000 vehicles and an expected first-year throughput of 180,000.
stories.headline: Barcelona port to build terminal to handle growing imports of Chinese cars

stories.body: Catalonia's government has commissioned a study for the first phase of the proposed Transversal Railway Axis, a cross-country line intended to link Lleida and Girona without passing through Barcelona. The initial study will examine a route from Lleida to Igualada and access to Barcelona, updating a project developed 17 years ago. The wider plan includes branches from Igualada toward Martorell, the Vallès and Barcelona, and toward Manresa, Vic and Girona; the government wants the route to carry freight as well as high-speed passenger trains.
stories.headline: Catalan government launches first phase of a new cross-country rail link between Lleida and Igualada

stories.body: Barcelona anti-fascist groups have called a counter-demonstration in Plaça Sant Jaume ahead of a planned Save Europe Act event at the same location. The groups say the far-right European movement promotes “remigration,” or the systematic return of undocumented migrants to their countries of origin, and allege links to Vox and ultra-conservative organisations. The counter-protest is scheduled for 18:00 on Saturday, an hour before the Save Europe Act gathering, while a Barcelona left-wing politician has urged city and regional authorities to prevent the event.
stories.headline: Anti-fascist groups call counter-protest against far-right Save Europe Act event in Barcelona
